insights.claim: The RHOAI distribution strips inline providers (docling, faiss, milvus-inline, sentence-transformers, pypdf, markitdown, docling-serve) from the upstream build.yaml, shipping only remote-capable providers suitable for multi-worker production deployments.
insights.reasoning: The config.yaml header documents stripped provider types. Comparing build.yaml (upstream) with config.yaml (distribution) shows inline::milvus, inline::faiss, inline::sentence-transformers, inline::docling, inline::markitdown, inline::pypdf, and remote::docling-serve are removed. This ensures the production image only uses remote backends compatible with horizontal scaling.

insights.claim: The entrypoint implements _FILE-suffixed secret resolution for 18 secret variables, enabling Kubernetes secret volume mounts as an alternative to environment variable injection to avoid /proc exposure.
insights.reasoning: The entrypoint.sh resolve_file_secret function iterates over 18 secret variable names and reads file contents into the base variable when the _FILE variant is set. This is a security-conscious pattern that avoids exposing secrets via /proc/1/environ.

insights.claim: OGX distribution acts as a multi-provider AI gateway supporting 8 inference backends, 3 vector databases, 2 search engines, and S3/local file storage, all conditionally activated via environment variable guards.
insights.reasoning: Each provider in config.yaml uses the ${env.VAR:+id} pattern to conditionally enable when the corresponding environment variable is set. This allows a single container image to serve diverse deployment scenarios without configuration file changes.
